title: Post-facto reconciliation and double-billing guards for dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: We need a robust post-facto reconciliation pipeline and preventative guards to stop double-billing and ensure accurate SLA crediting for Dedicated capacity customers. This ticket defines the problem, acceptance criteria, proposed design, migration plan, tests, and monitoring required to ship safe retroactive corrections.
details: Background: Dedicated pools reserve throughput (RPS/Tokens) and allow short bursts. Current production gaps: (1) transient race between the router and metering service can produce duplicated usage events during failover, (2) retroactive SLA credits triggered by partial pool degradations are not consistently applied to historical invoices, and (3) negative-balance corrections sometimes result in double-applying burst credits during reconciliations. These have led to 3 customer escalations in the last quarter and manual refunds.
goals: 1) Detect and dedupe double-emit usage events within a 72-hour reconciliation window. 2) Compute deterministic post-facto adjustments (credits/debits) tied to immutable reconciliation transactions. 3) Prevent double-application of burst credits during both live and retroactive reconciliation flows. 4) Provide audit trail and customer-facing explanation for any retroactive invoice adjustments.
non_goals: Rewriting the entire billing stack or changing pricing models. This ticket focuses on reconciliation correctness and guards only.
design_proposal: A. Event fingerprinting: add deterministic event_id computed from {tenant_id, pool_id, request_id, start_epoch_ms, model_id, billed_tokens}. Use event_id as primary dedupe key in metering store. B. Reconciliation ledger: append-only daily ledger entries for each tenant-pool with fields as CSV line: event_id, billed_amount_cents, billing_period, reconciliation_run_id. Ledger entries are immutable and the reconciliation runner will compute a diff against billed_state_snapshot. C. Idempotent credit applier: credits and debits issued by reconciliation will create a unique correction transaction with a stable correction_id composed from reconciliation_run_id and tenant-pool hash to ensure they are applied exactly once. D. Burst-credit flags: add a 'burst_origin' tag on credits (live vs reconciliation) and a guard in the credit-application path that prevents applying live burst credits to any invoice that has an overlapping reconciliation correction for the same token span.
schema_changes: MeteringEvent table: add columns event_id (STRING), reconciliation_tag (STRING), emitted_at_ms (INTEGER). Ledger store: new append-only CSV per tenant in GCS under gs://redwood-billing/ledgers/{tenant}/YYYY-MM-DD.csv. Correction table: correction_id (STRING), reconciliation_run_id (STRING), applied_at, reason, amount_cents. All schemas added as top-level fields in the billing DB migrations.
edge_cases: - Lost events: events arriving >72h will be marked late and audited but not auto-deduped. - Small rounding diffs between live and reconciliation totals: reconciliation runner will carry forward math to the cent and tag residuals for manual review. - Partial pool swap during reconciliation: if pool topology changed, reconciliation should attribute by time windows and use pool snapshots.
deployment_plan: 1) Schema migration to add event_id and correction table (backfill disabled) in staging. 2) Instrumentation rollout: router emits event_id for all requests; metering service validates format but falls back to legacy path if absent. 3) Run rehearsal reconciliation in QA/staging using 30 days of synthetic events. 4) Gradual rollout to prod with a shadow reconciliation pass for 7 days (no credits). 5) Enable idempotent credit applier in a canary subset of tenants (5%). 6) Full enable after 2 weeks of monitoring and manual signoff.
testing_plan: Unit tests for event_id generation and dedupe logic. Integration tests: simulate duplicate emits and verify single ledger entry. End-to-end test: inject failure during router failover and assert no duplicate billing. Rehearsal run against historical sample dataset to verify credit totals match expected manual calculation. Customer acceptance: run reconciliation shadow and sample invoices for 3 customers with high variance.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Dedup rate, late-event rate, reconciliation delta per tenant, number of correction transactions, average time-to-correct. Alerts: >0.1% daily dedup rate increase, reconciliation delta exceeding $5000 per tenant, correction-applier failures >= 5 in 1 hour.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reconciliation runner dedupes duplicate events with 99.999% success on test dataset. 2) Idempotent correction transactions are only applied once across retries. 3) No customer sees duplicate invoice line items after enablement. 4) Observability surfaces corrections with explanatory text for customers.
rollback_plan: If production reconciliation causes unexpected mass credits/debits, halt the correction applier and revert to shadow-only mode while we run manual diagnostic. For schema changes, use feature flags to avoid backfill until safe.
customer_communication: We will notify impacted tenants via email and console alerts with clear breakdowns of adjustments. Any corrective invoices will include a friendly explanation and contact link to billing@redwood.ai.
security_considerations: No PII added to ledger; ledger entries carry tenant_id but access controlled via billing service role. All correction operations require billing-service principal and are audited in Cloud Audit Logs.
open_questions: - Should late-arriving events (>72h) be eligible for automatic credits or require manual review? - Do we include model version in the event_id fingerprint to protect against rate-limited model switches? - How to present small < $1 residuals to customers (apply vs accumulate)?
